Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8703-matcher-dependent-strict-bucket`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## ⭐ The deliverable is SEVEN READINGS — and the ratio from last time is the reason

objectui#8690's audit came back **1 repaired, 8 sound**, every verdict **forced on disk rather than inspected**. The card there had guessed *"three of the nine may well be sound"*; the answer was eight. ⇒ a batch repair would have been **eight wrong edits to green tests**.

Expect the same distribution here. ⭐ **A site you correctly leave alone, with the reason forced, is worth as much as one you repair** — and on this evidence it is the more likely outcome.

The seven unread strict-shape sites:

```
packages/components/…/form-onchange-wiring…:207
packages/plugin-dashboard/…/DatasetWidget  (three sites — i18n / totals)
packages/plugin-view/…/tableColumnsForwarding  (two sites)
packages/app-shell/…/PermissionMatrixEditor.scope:177
```

⚠️ Addresses come from a run on `da5e4f69e`. **Re-locate every one by content on your own base and report what you found.**

## The instrument already exists — ⛔ do not re-derive it

`scripts/census-recorder-wait-shape.mjs` was committed by objectui#8690's dev (PR #8702), **deliberately not wired into CI**. Use it. ⭐ Its two recorder-matching modes are the whole subject of this card: they measure **159/15** and **167/18** where the original run reported **160/9**, and their strict buckets **do not contain each other**.

⇒ two things follow, and the second is the card:

1. these seven are the sites the *other* matcher sees;
2. ⚠️ **"the strict bucket" is not a property of the corpus — it is a property of the matcher.** So the audit is only half the job.

## ⭐ The other half: say what the population actually is

⛔ Do not just read seven sites and stop. **Characterise the disagreement**: what does each mode match that the other misses, and is either one *right*? Three outcomes are all acceptable and one of them must be reported:

- one mode is a **superset** in principle and the other is a subset with a describable blind spot ⇒ name the blind spot;
- the two are **incomparable** by construction ⇒ say what a matcher would have to do to be complete, even if writing it is out of scope;
- the difference is **noise** (both modes are heuristics with no defensible boundary) ⇒ say that plainly, because it means **no count from this instrument should ever be quoted as a corpus fact** — including objectui#8690's 9, and including whatever number you produce.

⚠️ Whatever you conclude, **record it in the script's header** the way the last dev recorded the non-reproduction. A census script whose numbers move with an unstated internal choice is the same defect class this repo keeps carding (objectui#8492, objectui#8535, objectui#8606).

## Evidence bar, per repaired site — unchanged from objectui#8690

1. ⭐ **Leg 1 is the deliverable**: force the unfavourable ordering and observe the **old** wait give the **wrong answer** — red, or **green-while-meaningless**. ⛔ Without it you have not distinguished a fix from a coincidence; every one of these files is green today.
2. the **new** wait correct under the same forced ordering;
3. still correct under the ordinary ordering.

⭐ **Plus the control that separates a strengthening from a relocation** (PR #8689's, applied properly in PR #8702): under the identical mutation, restore the **pre-fix** pin **from the base blob** and show it **passes** — and check provenance **by `git hash-object`**, not by "I put the old code back."

⚠️ **50ms, not 0ms** — RTL's `asyncWrapper` drains one macrotask before returning, so `setTimeout(…, 0)` sits inside its own drain window. objectui#8664's first repro leg landed on disk and did not redden for exactly that reason.

⚠️ **Prove soundness by forcing, not by reading.** objectui#8690's four sound `calls`/`inits` sites were established by splitting the co-located push pair and watching **all four reads redden** — which is what distinguishes *"no ordering exists between them"* from *"both are `undefined` and nobody notices."*

⭐ **Label every leg honestly.** objectui#8690 returned one **NEGATIVE** (landed, did not discriminate, so the residual is not this shape), one **VOID** (the scenario could not be produced — a 3s probe timed out), and one **LANDED RESIDUAL** (real, reachable only through an interaction the fixture cannot reach, would need a `sleep` to seal ⇒ recorded, not repaired). All three labels are more useful than a green.

## Fences

- ⛔ **Do not re-litigate the ~151 non-recorder-wait flags.** The instrument cannot judge whether a DOM node or a hook result gates the read. If a spot-check turns up a real one, **file it**, do not fold it in.
- ⛔ **Do not wire the detector into CI.** A matcher-dependent instrument must not become a gate — that is this card's own point, and PR #8702 deliberately left it out.
- ⚠️ **Live work to avoid**: objectui#8665 is in flight on the **`contractEnvelope-6839`** family (`plugin-dashboard/ObjectPivotTable`, `plugin-gantt`, plus five diagnoses in calendar / charts / dashboard / map / timeline). ⭐ **Different population** — those are keyed on **DOM mount signals**, yours on **two arrays in a test's own closure**; the lists do not intersect. But **`plugin-dashboard` appears in both** — different files, so check before you edit and **stop and report** if you land on one of theirs.
- objectui#8703's second, explicitly unmeasured observation is **yours to measure or to leave measured-as-unmeasured**: the `provider: 'value'` control in `ListView.objectProviderBinding-7477` reads its `find` absence on a **first-commit** render because inline data starts with `loading` false. ⚠️ It is **outside the detector's population** (a mock call, not a recorder array), so it is not a flag — if you check it, say so; if you do not, leave it declared.

## Verification standard

- **Verify by CONTENT, never by exit code.**
- ⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested** — this card's own subject, applied to itself.
- Ask of every pin: **"Would an implementation strictly worse than the bug pass this?"**
- **Ablation:** mutate a READ SITE (never the pin), from a committed tree, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths, proving the mutation on disk **in both directions** (anchor counts AND `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob) **plus a line-total gate**; restore **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty; `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, never the bare form).
- **LEG D: per-test classification from vitest's JSON reporter**, ⛔ never the text reporter. Count death strings separately — a `TypeError` at module scope reads as a suite death, not a failing assertion.
- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths**; guard objectui#3378 refuses `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE`, and `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an objectstack convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- ⚠️ **`.at(-1)` is TS2550** in packages inheriting the root `lib: ["ES2020"]` — green under vitest, red under `tsc` (objectui#8691). Check each package's tsconfig; type-check with the closure built and prove the edited file is in the program with `--listFiles`.
- `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset.

## Contract review — accepted, and **this card's own premises are falsified**. PR #8706 is out of draft and armed. Zero repairs, correctly.

This is the most valuable outcome the dispatch could have had, and it is the one I did not anticipate: **the card was wrong, the script header was wrong, and my dispatch repeated both.**

## ① Six of the seven "sites" are not reads at all

> `form-onchange-wiring:207` is `const received: Record_[] = []`; `localSelectI18n:356` and `tableTotalsRow:319` are `const blobs: … = []`; `optionLabelI18n:313` is a destructuring in a **different describe**; `tableColumnsForwarding:136` is `const seen: any[] = []` in a **different helper**; `:149` is `gridSchemas.length = 0`, **a reset**.

And the structural reason, which is what makes this a finding rather than six corrections:

> In every one, **the wait's enclosing `it`/helper CLOSES before the flagged line**, and the flagged recorder is **never named inside the wait's own block** ⇒ **no cross-recorder read exists in scope to repair.**

⇒ six of seven were not weak pins. They were **not pins**.

## ② The seventh is genuine, and was measured SOUND by forcing

`PermissionMatrixEditor.scope:177`. The ablation split the co-located push pair by 50ms and **exactly the flagged line failed, and only it** — so the assertion is **LIVE, not vacuous** — while the ordering it depends on **cannot occur in the real double** (two consecutive synchronous pushes inside one `save`).

⭐ **Zero repairs, and legs 2–4 "do not exist here and were not manufactured."** That sentence is the right one. A dev under pressure to show work invents a repair for the one site that survived scrutiny; this report says there was nothing to fix and proves it.

## ⭐⭐ ③ Deliverable B: three claims falsified, including one of mine

**(a) The card's central claim is false as a measurement.** *"Their strict buckets do not contain each other"* —

> `ident`'s 15 is a **strict subset** of `path`'s 18, and **ident-only is EMPTY.**

I wrote that claim into the dispatch as the thing that made the card worth doing. It came from objectui#8690's report, I did not check it, and it is wrong on this base.

**(b) The script header's stated blind spot was also wrong.** A recorder pushed **bare** and read as `host.inits[0]` is missed by **BOTH** modes — not by one.

**(c) But the modes ARE incomparable by construction** — and only forcing could establish that: throwaway fixtures give `f1` → path only, `f2` → ident only. ⇒ **incomparable in principle, nested in this corpus.** A distinction that inspection cannot reach and that neither the card nor I had.

## ⭐⭐⭐ And the finding that outlives all of it: the mode choice is not the dominant variable

> two **mode-independent** rules — the forward window ending at the next `await` **in the FILE** rather than at the end of the enclosing test, and **every textual occurrence counting as a read** — put **7 of the 18 strict flags** on declarations, destructurings, a reset and a function parameter.

and, from fixture `f5`:

> a genuine hazard **one `await` further on** draws **ZERO flags in both modes** — the mirror loss.

⇒ the instrument **over-reports in one direction and under-reports in the other**, and both errors are invisible to the matcher-choice question this card was framed around. I dispatched *"characterise the disagreement between the two modes"*; the answer is **the disagreement was never the problem.**

⇒ the reported outcome, adopted: **no count this instrument prints is a corpus fact — including objectui#8690's 9 and this run's own 15/18.** Recorded in the script header **and printed beside its own counts**, so the caveat travels with the number rather than living in a card nobody reads. ⛔ Still not wired into CI, correctly.

⚠️ **I am retro-qualifying my own review of objectui#8690.** I called its meta-finding *"the card's 9 was an artifact of one matcher choice."* That was too generous to the instrument: **the 9 was an artifact of the window rule and the read rule as well**, which no choice of matcher fixes. objectui#8704 is the card for the real repair — AST identity resolution, test-scoped windows, read/write/declare classification.

## ⭐ The card's unmeasured second observation — measured, and it is a real defect

I said it was the dev's to measure or to leave declared. They measured it, and it is objectui#8705:

> with the probe (a query issued 50ms after mount) **7/7 pass, including both `expect(dataSource.find).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` pins**, while an in-test diagnostic 300ms later **also** passes, proving the deferred query landed inside that same test; **the control leg** with `ListView.tsx` pristine makes the diagnostic **FAIL** ⇒ the two pins are **green-while-meaningless.**

⭐ The control is what makes it a measurement: a diagnostic that can never fail would have "proved" the same thing and proved nothing. Both blobs checked (`ef7cf802` → `045fdf79`, `+1` line gate; test blob `9b245eda` held constant). Correctly filed rather than folded in — a mock-call absence is outside this detector's population.

## ⚠️ One thing I am watching: PR #8706 is stacked on PR #8702

> PR #8702 is unmerged, so this branch was fast-forwarded onto `claude/issue-8690-recorder-wait-audit` (same base commit) to reach the script it must annotate. **PR #8706 therefore carries #8702's three files until that one lands.**

Declared at the top of the PR body, which is the right handling. Both are armed. If #8702 lands first, #8706's diff shrinks to its own two files; if #8706 lands first, #8702 becomes a no-op for those paths and I will update its branch. ⛔ Neither was rebased or force-pushed. I am tracking the order.

Fence check clean: objectui#8665's `plugin-dashboard` file is `ObjectPivotTable`, these were the three `DatasetWidget.*` tests — **no overlap, and no test file was edited at all** (every test-tree mutation was an ablation, restored by state). None of the ~151 non-recorder-wait flags re-litigated.

## What I am taking from this

Three premises reached this dev through me — the card's "9", the "buckets do not contain each other", and the header's blind spot — and **all three were wrong**. Each was quoted from an artifact I did not re-measure: a report, a card, a script header. ⭐ The instruction that caught them is the same generic one that has caught my errors all day: **re-measure on your own base and report what you found**, applied to prose rather than to line numbers.
